messages.author: 13d01984f5682713
messages.subject: algorithm
parts: I am a very new beginner for rstan, I referred to help(stan) today, and am confused about algorithm = c("NUTS", "HMC", "Fixed_param"). I know that stan uses Hamiltonian Monte Carlo sampling, so the basic algorithm in rstan should also be HMC. Then what does algorithm = c("NUTS", "HMC", "Fixed_param") mean? And I rstan, the default is NUTS, does this mean that if i want to use HMC to sampling, I need to add algorithm = c("HMC") in my stan() code? Thank you a lot.

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: algorithm
parts:
On Friday, March 24, 2017 at 10:02:25 AM UTC-4, Ru Wang wrote:
I am a very new beginner for rstan, I referred to help(stan) today, and am confused about algorithm = c("NUTS", "HMC", "Fixed_param"). I know that stan uses Hamiltonian Monte Carlo sampling, so the basic algorithm in rstan should also be HMC. Then what does algorithm = c("NUTS", "HMC", "Fixed_param") mean? And I rstan, the default is NUTS, does this mean that if i want to use HMC to sampling, I need to add algorithm = c("HMC") in my stan() code? Thank you a lot.

You don't want to use (static) HMC; you want to use NUTS (which is the default) because the number of leapfrog steps it takes on each iteration is not fixed. By leapfrogging until it reaches the u-turn point, you get better exploration and less dependence between draws.

Ben

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: algorithm
parts:
Notationally, "NUTS" refers to the No-U-Turn sampler which is an extremely efficient implementation of Hamiltonian Monte Carlo and the best option for almost every application, hence it being a default.

The "HMC" algorithm in RStan refers to static HMC, sometimes called vanilla HMC, which is the original but less efficient implementation of the Hamiltonian Monte Carlo method.  Sorry for the confusing notation -- we'll be sure to change it when we evolve the interfaces.

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: algorithm
parts:
On Friday, March 24, 2017 at 11:00:33 AM UTC-4, Ru Wang wrote:
So in this sentence "algorithm = c("NUTS", "HMC", "Fixed_param")" , HMC means (static) HMC, and both (static) HMC and NUTS are implementations of HMC?
Yes. It also means that dynamic HMC (NUTS) is the default.

I one more question. If I set chain=4 in one run time, I don't need to set seed values and I can still get four different sample chains. However, if I want to run for 4 times and each time with chain=1, then I need to set seed values for each time to get different sample chains?

You can and should set the seed to be the same thing each time but also set the chain_id to be 1, 2, 3, or 4. Then the results will be different. But honestly there is no reason to not just run it once with chains = 4.

Ben

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] algorithm
parts:
If you have four cores and enough memory, then you can run all
the chains at the same time. They'll all finish when the slowest
chain finishes. Chains don't all run at the same speed---they're
random processes, and can vary in run time substantially, particularly
in models with problematic geometry.

- Bob
